subject.title: exec private-LAN access fails while same user GUI/LaunchAgent succeeds

question: Should #94032 be resolved as a diagnostic-only exec warning, or should OpenClaw change private-LAN reachability semantics for gateway-host exec?
rationale: Source inspection shows the missing diagnostic, but allowing or intentionally blocking private-LAN exec traffic is a security-boundary and product-policy choice that automation should not make.

options.title: Land Diagnostic Only
options.body: Review and land #94045 after normal maintainer checks while leaving broader private-network access policy to related security trackers.

options.title: Design Access Parity
options.body: Treat same-user GUI/LaunchAgent parity as the product goal and require a separate security design before implementation.

options.title: Defer To Broader Trackers
options.body: Reject the diagnostic-only scope and keep this behavior under the existing private-network policy issues.

recommendation.title: Land Diagnostic Only
recommendation.body: Review and land #94045 after normal maintainer checks while leaving broader private-network access policy to related security trackers.

likelyOwner.reason: The current exec runtime/docs surface and deeper exec host-routing history most consistently route through this owner signal.
